{{Top|sprot}} {{Quote|Slavery, the most despicable of trades.|[[Police officer]] [[Exantor Divo]]|''[[Star Wars: Scum and Villainy: Case Files on the Galaxy's Most Notorious]]''}} [[File:ZygerrianSlaveAuction-SaV.png|thumb|right|250px|The Royal Slave Auction on Zygerria]] '''Slavery''' was an institutionalized practice where [[Sentience|sentient]] individuals were considered property who could be traded and held by other beings. '''Enslaved''' individuals were often called '''slaves''' and forced to perform labor for their [[enslaver]]s, who were also known as "owners" or "masters" and included those those who captured other people in order to "sell" as slaves.''[[The Rebellion Begins]]'' The [[Galactic Republic|Old Republic]] [[Judicial Forces]] worked alongside the [[Jedi]] to dismantle the [[Zygerrian Slave Empire|Zygerrian slave trade]],{{BuildFalconCite|91|Guide to the Galaxy}} but although slavery was outlawed in the [[Democracy|democratic]] Republic, gangsters such as the [[Hutt Clan]] continued practicing slavery beyond the Republic's reach on [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]] [[planet]]s such as [[Tatooine]].{{Film|I}} While the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] wrote in their [[Declaration of Rebellion]] that the beings of [[the galaxy]] were "born free under the auspices of nature," the authoritarian [[Galactic Empire]] targeted non-[[human]] [[species]] such as the [[Wookiee]]s to be secretly enslaved as unwilling laborers.''[[Star Wars Propaganda: A History of Persuasive Art in the Galaxy]]'' The Empire also worked with criminal syndicates such as the [[Pyke Syndicate|Pykes]] at the [[spice mines of Kessel]], where enslaved organics were chained and enslaved [[droid]]s had [[restraining bolt]]s installed, forced to risk their own lives to harvest for the dangerous [[spice]] trade. The Rebellion successfully built the [[New Republic]], and though its reach did not extend to criminal underworld havens such as [[Kijimi City]] by the time of the [[First Order]] conquest, even the anarchic [[city]]'s criminals did not welcome enslavers, who were afforded no safe quarter.''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary]]'' '''[[Indentured servitude]]''' was a nominally distinct practice in which sentient individuals performed labor for a fixed time period or until a specific amount of debt was paid off; after which point, they would be freed. However, in practice, indentured servitude typically amounted to slavery. Beings working in indentured servitude were called '''indentured servants''', though that term was often a euphemism for "slave."''[[Rebel Rising]]'' Another euphemism for "slave" was the term "'''sentient property'''," which the [[Czerka Arms|Czerka Corporation]] used in official documents to grant a veneer of legitimacy to their practice of slavery.''[[Master & Apprentice]]'' ==Characteristics== {{Dialogue|Omega|What's a slave trader?|Tech|Someone who buys and sells people for credits.|Omega|People can be sold?|Echo|They don't have a choice. They're captives, treated like property.|attr=[[Omega]], [[Tech]], and [[Echo]]|src={{TBB|Rampage (episode)}}}} [[File:JabbaLeia.jpg|thumb|left|230px|An enslaved Leia Organa forced to wear a dancing-girl outfit.]] Slavery was often used as a means for labor. The [[Galactic Empire]] enslaved [[Wookiee]]s because of their strength and ability to work long hours and in extreme conditions. Some [[Hutt]] [[crime lord]]s would enslave female [[humanoid]]s and force them to wear revealing [[dancing-girl costume]]s as entertainers.{{Film|VI}} [[Twi'lek]]s in particular were sought-after by slavers because they were generally considered beautiful.{{Databank|twi-lek|Twi'lek}} [[Youngling|Children]] born to enslaved (or indentured) [[parent]]s were considered to be slaves (or indentured servants) to the same master as their parents. Slave owners could free their slaves at will, and even [[Marriage|marry]] them, although marrying one's former slave was extremely uncommon. Notably, [[Cliegg Lars]] purchased, freed and then married [[Shmi Skywalker Lars|Shmi Skywalker]], the mother of Jedi Knight [[Anakin Skywalker]].{{Film|II}} The death of a slave owner could sometimes result in freedom for their slaves as well. [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] achieved freedom by killing her captor, [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure|Jabba the Hutt]], which also led to several of the gangster's other slaves gaining freedom. [[File:AnakinSkywalkerEpI-SWBC52.png|thumb|right|200px|Anakin Skywalker was born into slavery.]] Various methods were used to keep enslaved individuals from escaping or defying their masters. Some slaves had [[transmitter chip]]s implanted in their bodies that would explode if they tried to escape.''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know]]'' Others, were fitted with collars around their necks. Some collars were attached to chains that would be held by the slave's master. [[Zygerrian]]s commonly used [[shock collar]]s, which were used to electrocute slaves in order to force them to submit.{{TCW|Slaves of the Republic}} In many cases, those that were not actually enslaved in name nevertheless worked in near slave-like existences, forced to endure grueling jobs to eke out a meager living while also often having to contend with corrupt Imperial officials. [[Identity contract]]s, commonly called "ident pads," were used to identify individuals as indentured servants or slaves. Indentured servants and enslaved individuals could be put on trial for revolting against their masters. ==History== ===Slavery in the Old Republic=== {{Quote|Long have Sith empires been built upon the backs of slaves.|[[Darth Sidious]]|{{TCW|Escape from Kadavo}}}} Traditionally, ancient [[Sith Empire|empires]] controlled by the [[Sith]] relied on enslaved beings for labor. During the reign of the [[Galactic Republic|Old Republic]], [[Zygerria]] controlled a powerful [[Zygerrian Slave Empire|Slave Empire]]{{Databank|zygerrian|Zygerrian}} that stretched across a number of [[sector]]s,{{SWE|characters|queenmirajscintel|Queen Miraj Scintel}} making the [[planet]] rich and powerful. They and their customers prospered off slavery for thousands of [[Standard year|years]], but the [[Jedi Order]] eventually [[Jedi–Zygerrian conflict|fought and destroyed]] the Zygerrian slave trade.{{TCW|Kidnapped}} When slavery was outlawed in Republic territory, the [[Jedi Knight]]s liberated numerous beings, and the trade was pushed into the underworld. Although their influence was greatly diminished, the Zygerrians continued to operate in the slave trade through the [[Zygerrian Alliance]], which publicly was a guild of legitimate business. After the alliance backed a [[Insurrection on Aaloth|coup]] on the planet [[Aaloth]], the heir to the [[Keeper of Aaloth]] title, [[Lourna Dee]], was sold into slavery and brought to a [[Unidentified Zygerrian camp|Zygerrian camp]]. Later, however, [[Jedi Master]] [[Oppo Rancisis]] led a [[Attack on the Zygerrian camp|raid]] on the camp and freed those within. Eventually joining with the [[Nihil]] [[Pirate|marauders]], Dee helped take control of Aaloth to place it in Nihil hands. Despite that battle,''[[The High Republic: Tempest Runner]]'' the Nihil established relations with the Zygerrians and sold slaves to them.''[[The High Republic: Mission to Disaster]]'' ===Fall of the Republic=== {{Quote|I can't believe there's still slavery in the galaxy. The Republic's anti-slavery laws—''"''
''"''The Republic doesn't exist out here. We must survive on our own.|Padmé Amidala and Shmi Skywalker discuss slavery on Tatooine|}} Although the Galactic Republic had outlawed slavery, locations outside Republic jurisdiction were able to continue the practice. The [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]] planet of [[Tatooine]] had an enslaved population living in [[Mos Espa]], and slaves had [[transmitter chip]]s implanted into their bodies that would explode if the slave attempted to escape. By [[40 BBY]], [[Hosnian Prime]] was known for hosting a [[Hosnian Prime factory complex|factory complex]] run by the arms manufacturer [[Czerka Arms]], whose activities included the use of slavery, taking forcefully all the workers they wanted. Also, the [[Neimoidian]]s used indentured [[Neimoidian drone|worker drones]], whose growth was deliberately stunted. Such drones were even employed by the [[Trade Federation]]'s [[senator]]ial delegation in the very heart of the Republic's [[Imperial Senate Building|Senate Building]].[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2016)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']] In [[32 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' individuals like Anakin Skywalker, Shmi Skywalker, [[Wald]], [[Kitster Banai]], and [[Erdan]] were enslaved in Mos Espa.''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary, New Edition]]'' The [[Yam'rii]], an avaricious [[insect]]oid species from{{EncyclopediaCite|The Separatists}} the desolated{{ShipsandVehiclesCite|55|History of the Ship}} planet [[Huk]], had ruthlessly invaded numerous worlds in their [[Huk system|sector]], stripping them of their resources and selling their populace into slaves, and turned their attention to [[Kalee]], the inhabitants of the [[Reptile|reptilian]] [[Kaleesh]] species, with tempting results. [[File:TogrutaSlaves-SoR.png|thumb|left|300px|Enslaved Togrutas on Kadavo]] During the [[Clone Wars]], fought between the Republic and [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]], the [[Grand Army of the Republic]] was made up of loyal [[clone trooper]]s, [[Clone Sergeant]] "[[Slick]]," however, came to believe that the [[Cloning|clones]] had been enslaved by the [[Jedi]] Order, though he was taken into [[Prisoner|custody]] during the [[Battle of Christophsis]].{{TCW|The Hidden Enemy}} By [[20 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' [[Queen]] [[Miraj Scintel]] took advantage of the fighting to revive the Zygerria's ancient slave empire. Striking a deal with Separatist leader [[Count]] [[Dooku]], Zygerrian forces under [[Commander]] [[Darts D'Nar]] [[Battle on Kiros|enslaved]] the [[Togruta]] colonists on the [[Expansion Region]] world of [[Kiros]]. In response, the Jedi [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]], Anakin Skywalker, [[Ahsoka Tano]], and [[Clone Captain]] "[[Rex]]" undertook an [[Mission to Zygerria|undercover mission]] to Zygerria in an attempt to investigate the Zygerrians and free the Togruta colonists.{{TCW|Slaves of the Republic}} However, they were captured by Queen Scintel, who planned to enslave her Jedi captives. Since this went against the Sith's planned [[Great Jedi Purge]], Scintel was murdered by Count Dooku. Jedi and Republic forces subsequently managed to [[Battle of Kadavo|rescue]] some of the enslaved Togruta from the [[Kadavo slave processing facility|slave processing facility]] on [[Kadavo]]. In addition, Republic forces destroyed the Kadavo slaving facility. ===Age of the Empire=== {{Quote|I'm not completely comfortable with the idea that the Empire is using slaves, sir.''"
"''Terms are not always as they seem, Commander. They are called slaves, but they may in fact be indentured servants. They may be prisoners working off their sentence. They may have sold themselves into slavery as a means of repaying debts to others on their world. I have seen all those situations at times.|Eli Vanto and Thrawn discuss slavery|[[Thrawn (novel)|''Thrawn'']]}} [[File:LukeFindsCymoonCage-2015StarWars1.png|thumb|right|250px|Luke encounters enslaved aliens on Cymoon 1]] During the early years of the Galactic Empire, Zygerrian raiders attacked [[Syngia Station]] in the [[Sertar sector]] and enslaved many of the inhabitants. [[Penn Zarang]], who later became an [[Imperial cadet]] at the [[Arkanis Academy]], survived the slave raid by hiding in a maintenance conduit. The [[Death|murder]] of his [[Penn Zarang's father|father]] and the death of his [[Penn Zarang's mother|mother]] while en-route to Zygerria convinced Penn to become an Imperial [[cadet]]. The raid occurred at a time when the [[Imperial Military]] had not expanded into the Outer Rim.''[[Servants of the Empire: The Secret Academy]]'' During the [[Imperial Era|Age of the Empire]], slavery once again became commonplace, particularly among [[alien]] [[species]], which were considered [[Xenophobia|inferior]] by the [[human]]-dominated [[Galaxy|Galactic]] Empire. With the rise of the Empire, the softening and eventual repeal of laws outlawing slavery led to the classification of some species, such as the Wookiees, as non-sentient. As a result, the Wookiees were pressed into slavery building much of the Imperial war machine, or serving in the notorious [[Spice mines of Kessel|spice mines]] of [[Kessel]] following the Empire's [[Occupation of Kashyyyk|conquest]] of their [[homeworld]] of [[Kashyyyk]].''[[Star Wars Rebels: The Visual Guide]]'' Another example were the reptilian [[Bodach'i]] species who were enslaved and forced to work in the spice mines of [[Kerev Doi]] as "reparations" for their homeworld's repeated defiance of Imperial decrees.''[[Lost Stars]]'' In addition, the Empire used slaves from several alien species to keep [[Weapons Factory Alpha]], the largest weapons factory in [[the galaxy]], on [[Cymoon 1]] running [[Standard day|day]] and night.[[Star Wars (2015) 1|''Star Wars'' (2015) 1]] Around [[18 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' places the main events of ''[[Thrawn Ascendancy: Lesser Evil]]'' in [[18 BBY]]. followers of the [[Kilji way of order and enlightenment]] were slaves of their [[Kilji]] masters, as they could not move, or create any thought without them.''[[Thrawn Ascendancy: Lesser Evil]]'' After being given command of the [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]] ''[[Chimaera]]'', [[Commodore]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo|Thrawn]] discovered that the Empire was trafficking Wookiee slaves after responding to a distress call from the troop transport ''[[Sempre]]''. The slaves had been liberated by an attack force consisting of the frigate ''[[Castilus]]'' and two squadrons of [[V-19 Torrent starfighter]]s. The insurgents then launched an attack on [[Baklek Base]]. Thrawn led a successful military operation to neutralize the insurgents, forcing their surrender. When [[Lieutenant Commander]] [[Eli N. Vanto|Eli Vanto]] expressed his unease about slavery, Thrawn tried to rationalize the Empire's actions. ====Slavery under the Grysk Hegemony==== {{Quote|They are a terrible enemy, Eli. Your Empire—your ''former'' Empire—forces its will on its slaves through soldiers and weapons and warships. But the Grysks… three can command a nation. A hundred can rule an entire world. Billions of beings, their hearts and souls broken, ready to fight and die at the order of a handful of aliens. No resistance, no revolt, no dissent, no hope.|Navigator Vah'nya to [[Eli N. Vanto|Eli Vanto]]|''[[Thrawn: Treason]]''}} During the [[Grysk conquests]] in the [[Unknown Regions]] and the subsequent [[Imperial–Grysk conflict]], the [[Grysk Hegemony]] kept large numbers of slaves to further their conquests and even fight their battles for them. Often, the [[Grysk]]s enslaved entire species, by finding their weaknesses and breaking their souls. The Grysks sought to conquer the [[Chiss Ascendancy]] by enslaving and torturing the [[Chiss]]' beloved ''[[Sky-walker|ozyly-esehembo]]'' navigators. Among the species enslaved by the Grysks were the [[Darshi]]''[[Thrawn: Alliances]]'' and the [[Agbui|Scratchlings]]. After the rescue of navigator [[Un'hee]], who had been enslaved to the Grysks, by Imperial forces; her fellow navigator [[Vah'nya]] touched her mind through [[Telepathy|Second Sight]]. Vah'nya told Lieutenant [[Eli N. Vanto|Eli Vanto]] that she experienced the Grysks probing Un'hee's mind and soul, twisting and tarnishing the young girl's deepest desires and fears to force her to perform their will. She convinced Vanto that such enslavement was a fate worse than death, and asked Vanto to [[Death|kill]] her and any other ''ozyly-esehembo'' if they should fall into Grysk captivity. Killing a Chiss navigator was a [[Death penalty|capital offense]] in the [[Chiss Ascendancy]], so deeply ingrained in Chiss society that no Chiss could even conceive of killing a Chiss navigator. Vanto promised that, if it came to it, he would kill captured ''ozyly-esehembo'' to spare them the misery of Grysk slavery, and do so in a way that would kill as many Grysks as possible along with the navigators. ====Galactic Civil War==== {{Quote|But since that has ended, the breeding programs have become problematic. We have a surplus of slave labor—but what to do with it? Could the Wookiees be farmed for their meat? Presently it's stringy and tough, but maybe if they could be fattened up, or modified in some way—crossbred with another species, perhaps, like the Talz.|Commandant Theodane Sardo|''[[Aftermath: Life Debt]]''}} [[File:RodianFreeingEnslaved.png|thumb|left|200px|A female Rodian works to free slaves on [[Sclavos]].]] In [[4 ABY]], [[Princess]] Leia Organa was captured and enslaved by Jabba the Hutt during her attempt to [[Rescue of Han Solo|rescue]] [[Han Solo]]. However, Organa freed herself by killing the gangster, and in doing so, freed many of Jabba's other slaves. Because of this, she gained the admiration of the [[Nikto]]s, a species that had been prominently enslaved by the Hutts. Jabba's death also had a profound effect in the criminal underground as it both weakened the Hutt clan, and left a power vacuum on Tatooine and the Kessel spice trade routes.''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary]]'' Following the [[Battle of Endor]], the [[New Republic]]'s provisional [[New Republic Senate|Galactic Senate]] in [[Chandrila]] diverted substantial resources to compensating alien species that had been enslaved by the Galactic Empire. In [[5 ABY]], Han Solo and [[Chewbacca]] led a successful uprising of enslaved Wookiees on Kashyyyk against [[Grand Moff]] [[Lozen Tolruck]], the leader of [[Imperial territory G5-623]]. One of Tolruck's subordinates, [[Commandant]] [[Theodane Sardo]], toyed with the idea of farming enslaved Wookiees for their meat. As part of the plan, the former Imperial [[loyalty officer]] [[Sinjir Rath Velus]] disabled the [[Behavioral modification biochip|inhibitor chips]] controlling the enslaved Wookiees with a hyperspace transceiver spike. Following a battle on the ground and space above Kashyyyk, the planet was [[Liberation of Kashyyyk|liberated]] by New Republic forces led by [[Admiral]] [[Gial Ackbar|Ackbar]] and Leia Organa. Wookiee and New Republic forces later liberated more Wookiee slaves, including Chewbacca's son [[Lumpawaroo]], in mopping-up operations against Imperial holdouts on Kashyyyk.''[[Aftermath: Empire's End]]'' ===Post-Galactic Civil War=== {{Quote|I do not understand why you keep these... people, Agent Terex.''"
"''Oh, each of these folks is particularly, specifically useful to me, Phasma.|Captain Phasma questions Agent Terex about his slaves|[[Poe Dameron 1|''Poe Dameron'' 1]]}} Despite the New Republic's ban on slavery, seedy places like [[Chrome Citadel]] still exported enslaved individuals to [[Nal Hutta]] under the classification of "live cargo." In addition, individuals were still known to be indentured as servants. During an undercover [[Mission to Sibensko|mission]] to [[Sibensko]], [[Senator]] Leia Organa assumed the identity of a recently-freed indentured servant.[[Bloodline (novel)|''Bloodline'']] During the [[Hunt for Lor San Tekka|search]] for the explorer [[Lor San Tekka]], the [[First Order]]'s [[First Order Security Bureau|Security Bureau]] [[Agent]] [[Terex]] owned several enslaved beings from various species, including an [[Abednedo]] and a [[Rodian]]. He justified his behavior on the grounds that each of these aliens served a particular use and that the Empire practiced slavery, citing the enslavement of the Wookiees as one example. [[Captain]] [[Phasma]] disapproved of his ownership of slaves and regarded the First Order as purer and stronger than the Empire.[[Poe Dameron 2|''Poe Dameron'' 2]] ==Behind the scenes== Slavery first appeared in the [[1983]] film [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']], the third installment of the ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[original trilogy]].{{Film|VI}} In the early versions of ''Return of the Jedi'', the [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station|second Death Star]] was to be built in [[orbit]] around Kashyyyk. The construction would be done by Wookiee slave labor. [[George Lucas]] then decided to switch the Death Stars's location to the [[Endor|forest moon of Endor]] and the Wookiees were replaced with [[Ewok]]s.{{SW|url=news/much-to-learn-you-still-have-8-things-you-might-not-know-about-wookiees|text=Much to Learn You Still Have: 8 Things You Might Not Know About Wookiees}} In the drafting for the young-adult novel ''[[Queen's Shadow]]'',{{WebCite|url=https://toschestation.net/dragon-con-2019-e-k-johnston-and-claudia-gray-talk-the-prequels|text=DRAGON CON 2019: E.K. JOHNSTON AND CLAUDIA GRAY TALK THE PREQUELS|date=2019-09-14|format=[[Wikipedia:Podcast|Podcast]]|work=[https://toschestation.net toschestation.net]|archivedate=20200227051833}} released on [[March 5]], [[2019]],{{Disney|subdomain=books|url=book/queens-shadow|text=Queen's Shadow}} author [[E. K. Johnston]] worked with an editor to ensure the novel's inclusion of the concept of enslavement was written to use active wording rather than object words, specifically in regard to referring to someone as "enslaved" rather than "a slave." With the support of [[Lucasfilm Story Group]], she hired an additional editor to read over the novel's script, and also opted to use "souls" when referring to enslaved individuals to remind the reader that the individuals were indeed people. The novel ''[[Master & Apprentice]]'' by [[Claudia Gray]], released on [[April 16]] of the same year,{{PenguinRandomHouse|url=books/574531/master-and-apprentice-star-wars-by-claudia-gray/9780525619376|text=Master & Apprentice (Star Wars)}} similarly included slavery as a central theme in the work. She sought to include [[Jedi Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn]]'s encounter with enslavement on [[Pijal]]—in the form of meeting [[Rahara Wick]]—to add context to his actions in the [[prequel trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']]. Gray indicated that she also preferred using the term "enslavement" to refer to an individual's freedom status unless it was the enslaved individual referring to themselves as a "slave" or "former slave" in the proper context, to remain sensititve to the issue. In the usages of "slave" that she did keep in ''Master & Apprentice'', Gray noted that she included them to not word the concept too softly, indicating that evil individuals would not care about objectifying individuals and thus would choose to refer to individuals working for them derogatorily. ==Appearances== {{ScrollBox|content= *{{StoryCite|story=Gaze of Stone|book=Myths &
